probe: Change W2 copy_mode only; inspect saved config and ensure W1 unchanged.
why: The copy-model select is per-wallet and its value is live, not decorative: changing only W2's select from 'fixed' to 'proportional' and pressing Save rewrote live_config.json wallets[W2].copy_mode to 'proportional' while W1 stayed 'proportional' with unchanged numbers. Row-bound: it asserts THIS row's control writes THIS wallet's field; a different WTBL row (e.g. the Archive button) would not produce a copy_mode write. Note: the write to live_config.json (the engine's input) is proven; engine consumption is not exercised in the isolated instance. Independent review: cited evidence paths were present in the committed tree; exact content reviewed at b31edbf9b2f80037e1c6adb225bca0bc99d45e4b.

probe: Inspect live control inventory; check register-required B input is actually rendered.
why: Register expects the row to carry F/N/B inputs; the served build carries only two of the three. The wallet row's full control inventory is mode, copy_mode, fixed_notional, norm_base and its rendered inline labels are exactly 'F' and 'N' - there is no third (B) input, and the string user_norm_base does not appear anywhere in the served page. B (the user/base normalisation input the SSOT does still read at save_ui_state/effective_wallet_ui level) is therefore not settable from this table. Row-bound: the absence is specific to this row's control set and would fail for WTBL-09, whose control is present. Independent review: cited evidence paths were present in the committed tree; exact content reviewed at b31edbf9b2f80037e1c6adb225bca0bc99d45e4b.

probe: Mutate W2 F/N, save, reload, and compare W1 for unintended edits.
why: Save persisted the exact edited values for the edited wallet only and the values survive a reload, i.e. they come from disk and not from the form. Row-bound: the assertion is on this row's Save action writing both F and N for W2 while leaving W1 untouched; a different action button does not write these fields. Independent review: cited evidence paths were present in the committed tree; exact content reviewed at b31edbf9b2f80037e1c6adb225bca0bc99d45e4b.

(Note: the post-click badge readback landed on the row that had reordered to first position, i.e. W2 - the discriminating evidence for this row is the live_config.json value plus the wallet-named status line.) why: Archive (confirm dialog auto-accepted) removed exactly the clicked wallet from wallets{}, moved it into archived_wallets{}, and the table dropped from 2 rows to 1 with the sibling wallet still rendered. probe: Compare each wallet exposure against its own ledger size×entry; check unavailable fields stay nonnumeric.
why: Per-wallet section A rendered from each leader's own ledger sleeve and the exposure figure is arithmetically row-bound to that wallet: 0.0123 x 61234.5 = 753.18 for the BTC sleeve and 0.456 x 2456.75 = 1120.28 for the ETH sleeve (mark price unavailable, so the app used entry - and said so). Unknowns render as '-'/'N/A' with a reason rather than 0, satisfying the unavailable-source negative test for this row. Independent review: cited evidence paths were present in the committed tree; exact content reviewed at b31edbf9b2f80037e1c6adb225bca0bc99d45e4b.

probe: Compare wallet-specific coin/side/size/entry and unavailable exchange cells.
why: Section B renders the full eight-column position table per wallet, and each wallet shows only its own sleeve (W1 -> BTC long 0.0123, W2 -> ETH short -0.456) with the ledger entry price carried through. The exchange-dependent cells are explicitly marked unavailable (mark 'n/a', uPnL '-', EXCHANGE MATCH pill EXCHANGE_UNAVAILABLE) instead of being rendered as 0. Row-bound: the coin/side/size triple would be wrong if the section were merged across wallets or column-shifted. Independent review: cited evidence paths were present in the committed tree; exact content reviewed at b31edbf9b2f80037e1c6adb225bca0bc99d45e4b.

probe: With no fills, check C-specific n/a empty state, not zero slippage.
why: Section C exists and, with no friction fills available, renders the explicit unavailable path - 'Total diff: n/a', 'Avg diff: n/a' and the sentence 'reference/fill comparison unavailable' - rather than a zero diff that would read as perfect slippage. Row-bound: this is the C section's own empty-state contract, and it fails for a different row's section (A/D/E/F each have distinct empty-state text captured in the same file). Independent review: cited evidence paths were present in the committed tree; exact content reviewed at b31edbf9b2f80037e1c6adb225bca0bc99d45e4b.

why: Section D renders its four counters from the send-attempt record and, with no send_attempts.csv rows present, states the reason ('no real copied fills yet') instead of implying clean execution. Row-bound: the section, its counter set and its empty-state sentence are D-specific; the sibling sections in the same capture carry different labels, so a misplaced or shared component would fail here. why: The COIN column renders the coin of each leader's own sleeve and stays aligned with its wallet row (BTC on the 0x1111 row, ETH on the 0x2222 row). why: Side is derived from the sign of the ledger sleeve and both polarities are exercised in the same render: +0.0123 -> LONG and -0.456 -> SHORT. Row-bound: a hard-coded side or a lost sign would break one of the two rows, so this cannot pass vacuously from a single sample. probe: Compare signed sizes against seed inputs and ledger-net rows.
why: The ledger size column reproduces the exact seeded sleeve values, including the negative sign, and agrees with the independent ledger-net summary table rendered on the same page. probe: Check for MASTER clearinghouseState oracle; isolated snapshot absent, exchange size is dash.
why: This row's assertion is equality between the Exchange size column and the MASTER clearinghouseState, and that oracle is genuinely absent: the isolated app instance has no exchange_account_snapshot_app.json and no reachable Hyperliquid MASTER clearinghouseState read (component: Hyperliquid info API clearinghouseState for the follower account, which is not wired in this isolated render), so the column can only show '-'. The app's behaviour on that absence is correct and is captured (EXCHANGE_UNAVAILABLE, not 0), but that negative path is shared with the other POS rows and therefore cannot certify this row. Not a tooling fault: the probe is complete and re-runnable, the exchange truth simply is not available here. Independent review: cited evidence paths were present in the committed tree; exact content reviewed at b31edbf9b2f80037e1c6adb225bca0bc99d45e4b. The claimed live exchange comparison remains unproved.

probe: Check exchange entryPx oracle; isolated snapshot absent; displayed entry is ledger-derived.
why: The row's contract is that the entry-price column equals the exchange entry price. What the build actually renders in that position is the engine ledger average entry (61234.5 / 2456.75, matching the seeded ledger), while exchange entry px is unavailable - component: Hyperliquid MASTER clearinghouseState entryPx via exchange_account_snapshot_app.json, absent in this isolated instance. Certifying equality with exchange truth is therefore not possible here, and I will not pass a ledger number as if it were the exchange number.
